strings: Glyphic Memorandum is an introductory task directing novice mages in Coldridge Valley to their local trainer inside Anvilmar. Entrusted to mountaineer Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons budding arcane practitioners to seek out the eccentric gnome Marryk Nurribit to begin their formal spellcraft studies.

While assisting mountaineer Sten Stoutarm with early duties across Coldridge Valley, newly arrived mages find themselves summoned by local arcane authority. Sten receives a written memorandum addressed to the fledgling spellcaster and passes it along, advising them to take a moment to read its contents and head inside the warmth of Anvilmar to meet its author.

The author of the memorandum is Marryk Nurribit, a gnome mage trainer stationed inside Anvilmar. Rather than drowning his pupil in dense theoretical lectures, Marryk offers straightforward, grounded advice: stay out of serious trouble, save coin for training and tavern drinks, and strictly avoid the radioactive disaster that is fallen Gnomeregan. With basic expectations set, Marryk stands ready to tutor newcomers in the arcane arts.
Sten Stoutarm, an Alliance mountaineer stationed in Coldridge Valley, hands you the memorandum after you assist him with his initial tasks.
who gives glyphic memorandum | sten stoutarm quest
Marryk Nurribit is a gnome mage trainer residing inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. He instructs fledgling mages in early spells and general arcane safety.
who is marryk | anvilmar mage trainer
Where can I find Marryk Nurribit?
Marryk is located inside the main hall of Anvilmar, the central dwarven outpost situated at the top of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh.
marryk nurribit location | where is the mage trainer in coldridge valley
Why does Marryk warn against visiting Gnomeregan?
Gnomeregan was recently overrun by troggs and contaminated by a catastrophic release of radioactive gas, making it perilous for any novice adventurer wandering Dun Morogh.
marryk gnomeregan warning | why stay away from gnomeregan
This quest is exclusively provided to fledgling mages starting their journey in Coldridge Valley to introduce them to their class trainer.
who gets glyphic memorandum | is this quest mage only
What does Marryk expect from his students?
Marryk keeps his demands simple: he warns his students to stay out of trouble, save enough silver to pay for their spells and buy him an ale, and keep far away from Gnomeregan.
marryk expectations | what does the trainer want

This missive marks your official introduction to arcane tutelage in Dun Morogh, connecting you directly with your starting trainer.
The seamless cooperation between Sten Stoutarm and Marryk Nurribit illustrates the close partnership between dwarves and gnomes sharing Coldridge Valley.
Marryk Nurribit is one of several gnome specialists who took refuge in dwarven lands following the fall of Gnomeregan to teach their traditional craft.

Tainted Memorandum is an introductory quest for fledgling gnome warlocks taking their first steps in Coldridge Valley. Passed quietly through Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons the neophyte to the shadows of Anvilmar to meet Alamar Grimm, who preaches self-reliance through dark power rather than trust in their dwarven hosts.

Even in the frozen outpost of Coldridge Valley, the practice of the dark arts is met with deep suspicion. While helping Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, young gnome warlocks receive a slipped note. Sten delivers it reluctantly, giving voice to the uneasy truce that allows warlocks in Alliance lands: 'watch yerself... your kind ain't too trusted 'round these parts.'

Upon answering the note, the warlock meets Alamar Grimm lurking inside the halls of Anvilmar. Grimm does not mince words regarding the gnomes' plight. To his eyes, conventional tinkering and ordinary magic failed Gnomeregan utterly, driving their people to near extinction and leaving them stranded as second-class refugees dependent on dwarf goodwill. Rather than praying to the Holy Light or putting faith in dwarven politics, Grimm urges his pupil to summon and master fiends who offer unconditional obedience.
It is a written message handed to novice gnome warlocks by Sten Stoutarm in Coldridge Valley. It directs them to seek out Alamar Grimm, the local warlock trainer in Anvilmar.
tainted memo | warlock note dun morogh | what is the memorandum
Why are warlocks distrusted in Coldridge Valley?

Dwarves and their Alliance allies hold traditional virtues like martial honor and the Holy Light in high regard, viewing demonology and shadow magic as inherently corrupt and dangerous. Gnome warlocks operate under a cloud of deep social suspicion.
why don't dwarves like warlocks | warlock prejudice anvilmar

Alamar Grimm is a gnome warlock trainer residing in Anvilmar. Bitter over the fall of Gnomeregan and the indignity of relying on dwarven charity, he instructs young gnomes in the binding of demonic minions to secure their own power.
alamar grimm lore | who is alamar
Why does Grimm criticize normal magic and technology?

Grimm believes that conventional engineering and accepted schools of magic failed the gnomes during the disaster at Gnomeregan, leaving them dependent on dwarf patrons who prioritize ties with humans over reclaiming the gnome homeland.
grimm gnomeregan view | why dark magic over engineering
Can dwarf warlocks receive this quest?
No. In Dun Morogh, only gnomes can practice the warlock path, making this summons exclusive to freshly arrived gnome practitioners.
dwarf warlock tainted memorandum | can dwarves be warlocks
Where does this quest take place?
The quest begins near Sten Stoutarm in Coldridge Valley and finishes inside Anvilmar, the central redoubt overlooking the valley in southwestern Dun Morogh.
where is alamar grimm | tainted memorandum turn in
alamar grimm | anvilmar | coldridge valley | dun morogh | gnome warlock | gnomeregan exile | sten stoutarm | tainted memorandum
This missive marks your formal entry into the warlock craft, framing demonic pacts not as madness, but as pragmatism born of survival.
Dwarven hosts tolerate these dark practitioners under their roof with obvious distaste and sharp wariness.
The memorandum reflects the deep underlying resentment felt by some exiled gnomes over their displaced status and reliance on Ironforge.

The Simple Sigil is an introductory summons directed to aspiring night elf warriors in Shadowglen. Delivered by Conservator Ilthalaine on behalf of the trainer Alyissia, it formally marks the recruit's transition into combat training to protect the fledgling boughs of Teldrassil.
A Call to Arms in Shadowglen

After proving their basic survival skills against the restless wildlife of Shadowglen, young night elf warriors receive an inscribed sigil passed through Conservator Ilthalaine. The token is a formal request from Alyissia, the local warrior trainer stationed at Aldrassil, bidding the novice to step forward and dedicate their martial strength to defending their people.

When reporting to Alyissia, she places the warrior's training against a backdrop of rapid and troubling changes. In just a few short years, the night elves have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, watched an insidious taint spread through forest beasts both near and far, and reconnected with ancient ancestral regions once thought lost, such as Feralas. In the face of these perils, capable defenders are urgently required.

Beyond martial discipline, Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for the world outside their sheltered glade. She advises recruits to withhold prejudice against outsiders arriving upon Teldrassil from other races. While cautioning that not every traveler acts from pure altruism, she emphasizes that allies are vital to the defense of the Kaldorei, urging her pupils to extend reasonable trust as they take up their role as protectors.
It is an inscribed token sent by Alyissia, the warrior trainer in Shadowglen, delivered to novice night elf warriors to summon them for formal combat instruction.
simple sigil item | what is this sigil | sigil of the warrior
Who sends you to find Alyissia?
Conservator Ilthalaine delivers the sigil and directs you to Alyissia after you complete your initial tasks maintaining the balance in Shadowglen.
who gives the simple sigil | quest giver simple sigil
Alyissia is located within the safe haven of Shadowglen, standing near the great trunk of Aldrassil where she trains aspiring night elf warriors.
alyissia location | where is alyissia | warrior trainer shadowglen
Why does Alyissia say warriors are needed right now?

Recent years have brought drastic challenges: the founding of Teldrassil, widespread corruption infecting local wildlife, and the rediscovery of long-lost lands like Feralas. Skilled combatants are required to shield the Kaldorei from these encroaching threats.
why do night elves need warriors | shadowglen warrior lore
What does Alyissia say about other races visiting Teldrassil?

She counsels against prejudice, explaining that outsiders of other races will soon visit Teldrassil's boughs. While acknowledging that not all arrivals are purely altruistic, she advises extending a measure of trust so they might assist in the tree's defense.
alyissia on other races | night elves and outsiders | alliance in teldrassil
What is the significance of mentioning Feralas?

Feralas represents ancient night elf lands that were long cut off or believed lost following the Great Sundering. Its rediscovery highlights how rapidly the Kaldorei are reconnecting with the wider world after millennia of isolation.
aldrassil | alyissia | feralas | ilthalaine | shadowglen | simple sigil | teldrassil | warrior
This quest marks your official beginning as a Kaldorei warrior, introducing you to Alyissia as your initial mentor in arms.
Alyissia's counsel reflects the night elves' early efforts to welcome other Alliance races to their boughs despite centuries of isolation.
The sigil speaks directly to the rapid changes surrounding the Kaldorei—from the planting of Teldrassil to opening their secluded home to foreign allies.

The Etched Sigil is a written summons delivered through Conservator Ilthalaine to young night elf hunters in Shadowglen. It calls them up the great boughs of Aldrassil to meet their trainer, Ayanna Everstride, and formally begin their path of archery and beastcraft.

After proving their early vigilance in defending Shadowglen, young kaldorei hunters are handed an inscribed token by Conservator Ilthalaine. Carried originally by a messenger from the hunter mentor Ayanna Everstride, the etched sigil directs the novice to climb high into the upper reaches of Aldrassil, where the trainers keep watch over the canopy.

Meeting Ayanna marks the formal start of a hunter's training on Teldrassil. She instructs novices in the dual arts of marksmanship and understanding the wild creatures of Kalimdor. Ayanna emphasizes that a true hunter must treat their beast companions with respect, maintaining awareness and humility in a world full of unseen perils.
It is an inscribed message sent by the hunter trainer Ayanna Everstride to direct promising night elf novices to her post atop Aldrassil.
etched sigil | what is this sigil | sigil item
She can be found on the upper terraces of Aldrassil, the great world-tree hollow in the center of Shadowglen.
where is ayanna | find ayanna everstride | ayanna everstride location
Who hands out the Etched Sigil?
Conservator Ilthalaine hands it to night elf hunters once they begin proving themselves by defending the local woodland.
who gives the quest | quest giver | where do i get etched sigil
She trains hunters in the traditions of marksmanship, beast management, and wilderness survival while warning them never to underestimate the dangers abroad.
hunter training | what does ayanna teach | why talk to ayanna
Why does Ayanna caution hunters about their pets?

She reminds her students that the wilderness harbors threats far more formidable than novice hunters realize, meaning a hunter must respect their companion animals rather than treat their abilities casually.
beast danger | why respect beasts | pet caution
Is this quest available to other classes?
No, the Etched Sigil is specifically an introductory class summons meant solely for night elf hunters.
can druids do this | is this hunter only | other classes
aldrassil | ayanna everstride | etched sigil | hunter | ilthalaine | shadowglen | teldrassil
This quest marks your official introduction to hunter mentorship in Teldrassil, opening the door to learning bow craft, tracking, and beast mastery.
For the kaldorei, hunting is a sacred discipline intertwined with natural harmony and reverence for Elune, rather than mere sport.

The Encrypted Sigil is an introductory summons directed to nascent night elf rogues arriving in Shadowglen. Carried by Conservator Ilthalaine on behalf of Frahun Shadewhisper, it directs covert operatives to initiate their training and heed the fragile peace threatening Kalimdor.

While younger night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those inclined toward stealth and subterfuge receive a quieter summons. The Encrypted Sigil arrives by runner from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Inscribed with ciphers meant solely for initiates of the trade, it instructs the bearer to decipher its contents and seek out Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to formally begin their instruction.

Frahun's message is more than a simple training appointment; it serves as a sober warning regarding the geopolitical realities of Kalimdor. With the Third War concluded, the peace between the Alliance and the emergent Horde remains paper-thin. In Shadowglen, rogue scouts and informers are urged to cultivate their eyes and ears early, monitoring potential threats and covert provocations that could spark renewed war across the borders.
It is a coded token sent by the rogue mentor Frahun Shadewhisper to new rogues in Shadowglen, directing them to report to him beneath Aldrassil for formal training.
what is this sigil | encrypted sigil quest | sigil item
Who hands the sigil to young night elves?
Conservator Ilthalaine delivers the sigil on Frahun's behalf once an initiate has proven basic competence in managing the local wildlife around the boughs of Shadowglen.
who gives quest | quest giver | conservator ilthalaine
Where can Frahun Shadewhisper be found?
Frahun Shadewhisper is stationed within the shelter of the Great Tree Aldrassil in Shadowglen, ready to instruct newly arrived night elf rogues.
where is frahun | find frahun shadewhisper | frahun location
Why are rogues needed in peaceful Teldrassil?

As Frahun notes, the prevailing truce with external factions is tenuous. Stealthy scouts and intelligence gatherers are vital for uncovering subterfuge, particularly concerning Horde movements and internal threats to the boughs.
why do night elves need rogues | rogues in shadowglen | purpose of rogues
What happens after presenting the sigil to Frahun?
Frahun accepts the cipher, acknowledges your readiness, and invites you to return as you gain experience so he can teach combat techniques, weapon handling, and the arts of stealth.
what comes next | after encrypted sigil | sigil reward lore
Does the Horde actively threaten Shadowglen directly?
While the remote canopy of Teldrassil is largely secluded from open Horde assault, whispers of Horde agents sowing distrust across Kalimdor keep kaldorei sentries and operatives on high alert.
is horde in teldrassil | horde threat shadowglen | horde seeds of distrust
aldrassil | conservator ilthalaine | encrypted sigil | frahun shadewhisper | rogue trainer | shadowglen | teldrassil
This task marks your entry into the kaldorei network of scouts, assassins, and intelligence gatherers tasked with protecting Teldrassil from unseen adversaries.
Shadowglen's trainers remind recruits that cross-faction treaties are fragile and that intelligence work is critical to preventing Horde incursions.
Even in the secluded haven of Aldrassil, the kaldorei maintain watchful eyes on Kalimdor's shifting borders to defend their newly planted boughs.

The Hallowed Sigil is an introductory summons delivered to young night elf priests beginning their training in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along the message from the priest trainer Shanda, directing novice practitioners to seek guidance within Aldrassil as they learn to wield Elune's grace.

Priests in night elf culture occupy a sacred place as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess, Elune. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows an affinity for the divine light and devotion, Conservator Ilthalaine entrusts them with a hallowed sigil. Sent by messenger from the priest trainer Shanda, the token serves as a formal invitation to present oneself at the tree of Aldrassil to begin dedicated spiritual tutelage.

Upon meeting Shanda, the young acolyte finds that the sheltered sanctuary of Teldrassil is experiencing unusual upheaval. Shanda notes that the boughs of the World Tree are stirring with travelers, including members of the wider Alliance granted leave to meet with the kaldorei. While the broader world calls, Shanda advises novices to ground themselves in the troubles immediately facing Shadowglen before venturing into the wider conflicts beyond.
It is an inscribed token sent by the priest trainer Shanda via messenger to Conservator Ilthalaine, meant to summon a novice priest for instruction in Aldrassil.
hallowed sigil item | what is this sigil | sigil of shanda
Shanda is the priest trainer stationed at Aldrassil in Shadowglen. She guides fledgling night elf priests in the fundamental rites, disciplines, and prayers of the Sisterhood of Elune.
priest trainer aldrassil | who is shanda
Shanda resides inside the hollow base of Aldrassil, the massive central tree at the heart of Shadowglen in Teldrassil.
find shanda | where to turn in hallowed sigil | shanda location
Why are Alliance members visiting Teldrassil?

The night elves have forged ties with the Alliance following the Third War. Outside races are beginning to arrive on Teldrassil's boughs to coordinate and confer with the kaldorei as both sides prepare for the challenges facing Azeroth.
alliance in teldrassil | why outsiders on world tree
What should a priest do after completing this task?
Shanda advises priests to assist the local defenders and caretakers across Shadowglen, returning to her whenever they need to learn new prayers and techniques.
what next after sigil | after hallowed sigil
Why does Ilthalaine give this quest?

Conservator Ilthalaine oversees the earliest trials of novices in Shadowglen. When a messenger from Shanda arrived with the sigil, Ilthalaine held it until the aspiring priest proved capable of taking their next steps.
conservator ilthalaine priest | why talk to ilthalaine
aldrassil | conservator ilthalaine | elune | hallowed sigil | priest | shadowglen | shanda | teldrassil
This rite of passage connects a novice kaldorei priest with Shanda, initiating their formal training in the light and wisdom of Elune.
Shanda's remarks highlight how newly established Alliance alliances are bringing unfamiliar races and travelers directly onto Teldrassil's boughs.
The priesthood is central to kaldorei culture, governed by ancient traditions of lunar devotion that have guided their people for millennia.

Tundra MacGrann, an injured dwarven hunter living out in the cold crags of Dun Morogh, has lost his winter supplies to a notorious local beast. A massive yeti known as Old Icebeard hauled off MacGrann's thorium-reinforced meat locker into its den. Unable to outrun the beast on a bum leg, the hunter relies on passing adventurers to slip inside and retrieve his provisions.

Surviving the harsh winters of Dun Morogh demands preparation, especially for mountaineers living outside the warmth of Kharanos and Ironforge. Tundra MacGrann had diligently salted away an entire month's worth of dried meats to outlast the coming cold season flurries. Taking precautions against hungry wild bears, he sealed his rations inside a reinforced thorium meat locker. Unfortunately, he did not account for the sheer brute strength of the mountain yetis, who carried the entire chest away rather than trying to open it on the spot.

The culprit behind the theft is Old Icebeard, a feared and vicious yeti lurking in the jagged hills. While MacGrann was away hunting deer, Icebeard snatched the chest and dragged it back to his mountain cave. Though MacGrann remains confident that even a yeti cannot shatter solid thorium plating, his own injured leg makes a recovery mission suicidal. Any brave soul venturing into the cave must either contend directly with the beast or time their intrusion carefully while the monster is out prowling the snowdrifts.
Tundra MacGrann is a dwarven trapper and hunter dwelling in the snowy expanses of Dun Morogh. Nursing a bad leg, he depends on his harvested stores to endure the harsh winter conditions.
tundra macgrann | macgrann | who is macgrann
A menacing local yeti known as Old Icebeard stole the locker while MacGrann was away hunting deer, dragging the heavy thorium chest into its mountain lair.
who stole the stash | who took the meats | stolen stash thief
Why can't MacGrann get his meats back himself?
MacGrann suffers from an injured leg that severely limits his mobility. He knows he cannot move swiftly or quietly enough to enter and escape Old Icebeard's cave without being caught and mauled.
why cant macgrann get it | macgranns leg | bum leg
Did the yeti eat the food?
No. The dried meats were locked inside a sturdy chest crafted from solid thorium. While the yeti succeeded in carrying the heavy container off, it is unable to break through the metal.
is the food eaten | can icebeard open the chest
Do you have to fight Old Icebeard to get the meat locker?
No, you do not necessarily have to fight him. Old Icebeard regularly wanders outside his lair, giving nimble adventurers an opportunity to sneak into the cave and loot the locker unnoticed.
can you sneak past icebeard | do i have to kill icebeard
Where is the stolen stash located?
The stolen meat locker rests deep inside Old Icebeard's mountain cave, located in the hills near MacGrann's camp in Dun Morogh.
where is the cave | icebeard cave location
dried meats | dun morogh | meat locker | old icebeard | stolen stash | thorium | tundra macgrann | yeti
Fellow trackers will sympathize with MacGrann's misfortune of having months of diligent field dressing and game preservation undone by an opportunistic beast while out tracking deer.
MacGrann specifically seeks out stealthy travellers, making this theft a textbook job for scouts who can slip in behind Old Icebeard's back without ever drawing a blade.
Every dwarf in Dun Morogh knows the unforgiving brutality of a mountain winter; without preserved meat or shelter, even a hardened mountaineer cannot hold out against the freeze.
Why does Tundra MacGrann need his meat locker recovered?

MacGrann spent long days hunting and salting an entire month's worth of rations to survive the harsh Dun Morogh cold season. Without those preserved meats, he faces starvation in his remote mountain camp once the winter flurries roll in, as his injured leg prevents him from hunting enough game to replenish his winter stores in time.
why help tundra macgrann | macgrann motive | why retrieve the meat locker

It is a heavy reserve of salted venison and game that Tundra MacGrann cured specifically to outlast the mountain winter. He locked the meat inside a reinforced thorium locker to keep scavenging bears from sniffing it out, which luckily proved durable enough to keep Old Icebeard from tearing into it as well.
macgranns dried meats | what is macgrann's dried meats | macgrann meat locker contents

The Verdant Sigil is a written summons delivered to newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes it along to direct fledgling shapeshifters to Mardant Strongoak within the boughs of Aldrassil. It marks the formal beginning of a druid's tutelage in the mysteries of nature and the Emerald Dream.

Once a young night elf shows promise in maintaining the local balance of Shadowglen, a formal introduction to their order is required. Conservator Ilthalaine receives the Verdant Sigil via a runner and entrusts it to the initiate. The small token signifies that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to formally begin their training.

Upon presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil, the initiate is welcomed into the fold. While deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastering animal forms lie ahead, Mardant establishes himself as their first guide, tasked with teaching them how to interpret nature's spirits and channel raw woodland power.
It is a inscribed summons delivered through Conservator Ilthalaine on behalf of Mardant Strongoak, calling a novice druid to begin their formal training inside Aldrassil.
verdant sigil item | what is this sigil | druid sigil
Where do I take the Verdant Sigil?
Bring it to Mardant Strongoak, the druid trainer stationed within the great barrow-tree of Aldrassil in the heart of Shadowglen.
where is mardant | turn in verdant sigil | where do i go
Why does Mardant mention the Emerald Dream?

Druids draw much of their power and wisdom from the Emerald Dream through long sleeping trances. Though a novice is not yet ready to wander the Dream freely, Mardant introduces it as the foundational mystery they will eventually study.
why emerald dream | mardant dream dialogue | druid trance
Who sends the sigil to Ilthalaine?
A messenger sent by Mardant Strongoak delivered the sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine so it could be placed directly into the hands of a promising young druid.
who sent the sigil | sigil messenger

Mardant Strongoak becomes your primary mentor in Shadowglen, allowing you to learn your earliest druidic spells and magical techniques as you grow in power.
what do i learn next | after verdant sigil
No. The Verdant Sigil is strictly meant for night elf druids beginning their journey in Shadowglen. Other classes receive their own distinct summons to their respective trainers.
is this druid only | who gets verdant sigil
aldrassil | druid trainer | emerald dream | ilthalaine | mardant strongoak | shadowglen | verdant sigil
This quest represents your formal initiation into the Cenarion circle's teachings under Mardant Strongoak, setting you on the long path toward understanding the Emerald Dream.
Druidism is deeply woven into night elf culture; presenting this sigil at Aldrassil marks the first step of an initiate stepping into an ancient tradition.

Pilot Stonegear of Kharanos is looking for someone with true dwarven grit to spruce up his beloved siege engine, Trollplow. To test an aspiring adventurer's mettle, he sends them west into the perilous cavern known as the Grizzled Den to hunt savage wendigos for their thick pelts.

Operating a massive dwarven siege tank requires nerves of iron and the constitution to handle teeth-rattling machinery in freezing mountain air. Pilot Stonegear, stationed at Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, claims to have both in spades. Rather than simply giving up work or respect easily, he challenges newcomers to prove they possess the same stalwart temperament by trekking into the frozen hills to face native beasts.

Stonegear's siege engine bears the proud and unsubtle name of Trollplow, but its cramped, iron-plated cabin is brutally cold in the bitter Dun Morogh climate. Stonegear hits upon a practical yet wild solution: wendigo pelt. Harvesting thick manes from the ferocious wendigos stalking the Grizzled Den provides the materials needed to fashion a durable, warm rug for Trollplow's deck while keeping local beast numbers in check.

Pilot Stonegear is a dwarven siege engine driver stationed outside Kharanos in Dun Morogh. He pilots an armored war machine affectionately christened Trollplow and takes immense pride in his iron nerves and mechanical trade.
pilot stonegear | who gives quest | who is stonegear
Where is the Grizzled Den located?
The Grizzled Den is a snow-covered cave system nestled in the mountains directly west of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for Dun Morogh's vicious wendigos.
grizzled den location | where is wendigo cave | how to find grizzled den
Why does Stonegear want wendigo manes?
Stonegear wants the thick, insulating fur of the wendigos to craft a cozy rug for the interior deck of his siege engine, Trollplow, while simultaneously testing an adventurer's bravery.
why wendigo manes | purpose of manes | what are manes for

Trollplow is Pilot Stonegear's personal dwarven siege engine. Its aggressive name reflects the ongoing conflict between Ironforge dwarves and the hostile Frostmane trolls that inhabit the surrounding crags.
trollplow | stonegear tank | what is trollplow
What kind of creatures inhabit the Grizzled Den?
The cavern is inhabited by savage wendigos—feral, ape-like beasts native to Dun Morogh's snowy heights that aggressively defend their territory from any who intrude.

Are the wendigos dangerous to Kharanos?

While wendigos rarely organize concerted attacks like the Frostmane trolls, their violent ferocity and proximity to the main roads make them an ever-present danger to travelers and local tradesfolk alike.

dun morogh | grizzled den | kharanos | pilot stonegear | trollplow | wendigo | wendigo mane
Anyone who appreciates the craft of dwarven siege vehicles knows that maintaining heavy machinery in sub-zero weather requires creative solutions for cockpit warmth.
For young Mountaineers and Ironforge adventurers, taking on the wendigos of the Grizzled Den is a quintessential local rite of passage.
Living side by side with the dwarves around Kharanos means pitching in to help equip Ironforge's heavy armored engines.
What are the Wendigo Manes used for?

Pilot Stonegear wants the thick, shaggy manes of the Grizzled Den's wendigos for a very practical dwarf luxury: interior decorating. Operating a massive siege engine like Trollplow in Dun Morogh's biting chill leaves the metal deck freezing underfoot. Stonegear plans to stitch the harvested manes together into a warm, heavy rug to make Trollplow's cabin much cozier during long patrols.
wendigo mane use | what is wendigo mane for | why wendigo manes
Why does Pilot Stonegear send you instead of getting the manes himself?

Stonegear is a siege engine pilot, and keeping an iron machine like Trollplow maintained and ready for defense in Kharanos demands his full attention. Hunting agile, ferocious wendigos inside tight, frozen cavern passages isn't work suited for a massive war machine. Stonegear also treats the task as an open challenge to see if you have the grit, mettle, and nerve required of Dun Morogh's defenders.
why me stonegear | why does stonegear need help | why not get manes himself

Protecting the Herd is a task given by Rudra Amberstill at the Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh. A ferocious predatory beast named Vagash has been attacking the ranch's prized mountain rams in the night, and with Ironforge's military garrison spread thin across the realm, the local breeders must rely on passing adventurers for defense.

Amberstill Ranch supplies the mountain rams that serve as iconic mounts and working beasts for the Bronzebeard dwarves. Maintaining these herds is vital to Dun Morogh's rustic economy. When night fell and frantic cries echoed over the paddocks, the Amberstill family discovered two of their prized rams missing. The culprit is Vagash, a notorious and savage beast lurking in the nearby crags above the ranch, known for violently preying on local livestock.

Normally, local threats of this magnitude would be handled by the dwarven mountaineers or King Magni Bronzebeard's royal forces. However, Ironforge's standing army is currently stretched thin across distant frontiers supporting the broader Alliance. Left without an official military detachment to patrol the ridgelines, Rudra Amberstill is forced to ask independent fighters to hunt down Vagash and bring back one of the beast's deadly fangs as proof.

Vagash is a dangerous, predatory monster that stalks the snowy ridges directly above Amberstill Ranch. Feared for his sheer strength and vicious appetite, he poses a lethal threat to both domestic ram herds and unwary travelers in eastern Dun Morogh.
what is vagash | vagash monster | vagash lore

Vagash makes his den in a snow-covered cave high up in the crags overlooking the Amberstill Ranch. Ascending the snowy hill just past the pine trees behind the homestead leads directly to the mouth of his lair.
vagash location | where is vagash | find vagash
Why are the Ironforge guards not handling this?

King Magni Bronzebeard's forces are currently spread thin defending strategic garrisons and supporting distant Alliance campaign efforts. As a result, rural homesteads like Amberstill Ranch must fend for themselves or recruit capable adventurers.

Why does Tyrion need you to carry out the attack instead of the guards?

Lord Lescovar is a high-ranking nobleman inside the royal court, and the Stormwind guards are bound by duty to obey and protect him.
